tells: 1. The close-up is a game cutscene: the face is a flat waxy orange with no pores, no specular breakup and no subsurface falloff, the nose and jaw are low-poly, and the eyes are painted with no wet catchlight from any practical in the room (club-4-face.png, centre face)

2. The front row is lit from nowhere: faces and jackets carry an even frontal fill brighter than the tealights on the tables could give, with no warm underlight from the candles on chins, hands or cups and no cast shadows on the tabletops (club-1-wide.png and club-3-mid.png, front row and tables)

3. The back of the house is flat black cut-out silhouettes of identical value against uniform haze, with no rim, no edge falloff, no depth of field and no partial light; it reads as a cardboard backdrop, not people in fog (club-1-wide.png, middle band behind row 1; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

4. Fake lens: the defocus in the close-up has a hard matte edge around the subject (a dark halo along the hair and shoulder) where a real lens rolls off gradually, and the wides have no lens behaviour at all: no flare or veiling from the wall sconces, no vignetting, no grain, clipped-black blacks (club-4-face.png, left of the hair and right shoulder; club-1-wide.png, whole frame)

5. The strip barely moves for the start of a laugh: across 1 s most bodies are frozen and only heads turn slightly; no one rocks back, no shoulders heave, hands stay locked on the tables like mannequins, and identical clothing (the magenta track top, the green hoodie, the white cardigan) repeats across shots (club-5-strip.png, all six frames; club-2-mid.png vs club-6-held.png, same people)

1. The wide is a grid of standing-height figures pasted on a black field: the rear rows float with no seats, no armrests and no floor, the people are evenly spaced in perfect lines and all lit to the same value regardless of distance from the stage (theatre-1-wide.png, rows 3 and up and the left block)

2. The close-up reads as a 2005 game render: the hair is a solid helmet of blonde texture with no strands at the hairline, the mouth interior is a black hole with no teeth or tongue, the eyes have no catchlight and the skin is uniform peach plastic (theatre-4-face.png, hair, mouth and eyes)

3. No motivated light: the stage spill should come from the stage at low angle and fall off front to back, but the front row is lit flat and frontally like a studio fill, while three bare hot points in the ceiling light nothing around them and produce no flare or haze cone (theatre-1-wide.png, the three ceiling dots and front row; theatre-2-mid.png, upper half)

4. Bodies don't sit in the seats: hips hover above the cushions, thighs pass into the seat backs, hands rest on knees in identical mannequin poses and the seats cast no contact shadow on the bodies (theatre-2-mid.png and theatre-3-mid.png, front row laps and seats; theatre-1-wide.png, front row)

5. The rear audience are cut-out silhouettes and low-detail impostors with a pale cut-out edge; the held frame shows a halo/ghost outline around the cap and hoodie and the defocused faces behind keep sharp texture with no bokeh, so the depth of field is a post blur, not a lens (theatre-6-held.png, edges of the cap and hoodie and the back row; theatre-2-mid.png, back rows)

1. The close-up hair dissolves into a stippled dithered fringe at the back of the head and around the ear, a clear alpha-test artefact, and the matte edge between the subject and the blurred background is hard and dark like a cut-out (openmic-4-face.png, right of the head and along the cheek and shoulder)

2. The light has no source: the faces are lit warm and evenly from the front at eye level while the only visible practicals are a row of downlights on the back wall that light no wall, no floor and no hair from behind; there is no top-light, no hot spots on heads, and the downlights have no halo cone in the haze (openmic-1-wide.png, back wall and audience; openmic-2-mid.png, top band)

3. The wide is a single packed clump on a black floor in an empty dark box: no chairs read, no floor plane, no shadows under the group, the back rows are flat silhouettes and the room geometry (the bright door slab at left, the ceiling soffit) is untextured (openmic-1-wide.png, lower third and left wall)

4. Faces are plastic: uniform skin without pores, shine or redness, painted eyes without moisture or catchlights, lips that open to a dark slot; the woman in green and the man in the red track top have rubbery, stretched features at mid range (openmic-2-mid.png, centre right faces; openmic-3-mid.png, right edge)

5. The laugh in the strip is a few head turns and mouths opening; torsos stay rigid on stiff spines, nobody throws back, claps or covers the mouth, and hands stay glued to the knees in all six frames, with clothes that never fold or crease with the body (openmic-5-strip.png, all frames, lower half; openmic-6-held.png, laps and hands)
